actions: elevates mandible (bite force, especially molar region)

functional_compartments.name: Superficial head
functional_compartments.function_note: Larger, more obliquely-oriented head arising from the zygomatic process of the maxilla and anterior 2/3 of the zygomatic arch.
functional_compartments.source: van Eijden TM, Korfage JA, Brugman P (1997) Anat Rec 248(3):464-474 -- architecture of the human jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid): fascicle length, pennation angle and PCSA by head/region

functional_compartments.name: Deep head
functional_compartments.function_note: Smaller, more vertically-oriented head arising from the posterior 1/3 of the zygomatic arch, partly covered by the superficial head.
functional_compartments.source: van Eijden TM, Korfage JA, Brugman P (1997) Anat Rec 248(3):464-474 -- architecture of the human jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid): fascicle length, pennation angle and PCSA by head/region

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); van Eijden TM, Korfage JA, Brugman P (1997) Anat Rec 248(3):464-474 -- architecture of the human jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid): fascicle length, pennation angle and PCSA by head/region

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse or longitudinal over the angle and ramus of the mandible, along the line from the zygomatic arch to the mandibular angle -- the classic 2-3-point injection strip for bruxism/masseteric hypertrophy sits in the lower, posterior two-thirds of this line.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Two layers: a larger superficial layer running obliquely from the zygomatic arch to the angle/ramus, and a smaller deep layer from the deep surface of the arch to the upper ramus and coronoid process. The parotid gland and duct overlie its posterior/superior part.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Bulges prominently on clenching -- the standard confirmation maneuver, and the reason masseteric hypertrophy from bruxism is so easily palpated before it is imaged.
structures_at_risk: buccal branches of the facial nerve, running across the superficial surface just deep to the parotideomasseteric fascia -- the reason injections stay in the lower two-thirds and avoid the anterosuperior corner of the muscle
facial artery and vein, and the parotid duct (Stensen's), crossing the muscle's anterior border near the level of a line from the tragus to the midpoint of the upper lip
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The muscle most commonly injected for bruxism, masticatory myofascial pain and masseteric hypertrophy, almost always alongside temporalis. A published pediatric case used 2 points per side (10 U each) guided by palpation and surface landmarks alone, without ultrasound or a stated percentage-based zone -- consistent with how most published technique in this muscle is described (by anatomical region, not a measured reference line).
